$comment: What a route may cost before the build refuses it.
THE GAP THIS CLOSES. The suite here notices WRONG behaviour from several angles —
the unit suite, the mutation drill (would a wrong answer be killed?), the flake drill
(does the suite answer twice the same way?) and a key-free Playwright lane that loads
whole pages. Not one of them notices SLOW behaviour. A change that doubles a route's
server time passes every gate in `npm run check:ci`, and the first thing that reports
it is a person waiting for a page. An agent optimising for a green gate has, until
this file, had no signal at all that a change cost anything.
WHAT IS MEASURED, stated so a green line is not over-read. `metric.what` is the
DOCUMENT RESPONSE: the wall clock from `page.goto` to the navigation committing, i.e.
the server answering the route with the HTML document. That is the number a server
change moves — a store read that stopped being deduped, an await added above a
Suspense boundary, a fan-out that used to be one query. It is deliberately NOT
DOMContentLoaded: in `next dev` the deferred chunks are unminified and megabytes wide,
so that number measures the dev bundler far more than it measures this repository's
code, and a budget over it would be noise with a threshold on it.
WARM, AND BEST OF THREE. The first hit on a route in `next dev` compiles it, which is
a fact about Turbopack and not about the page, so `metric.warmups` navigations are
thrown away before `metric.samples` are kept and the MINIMUM is compared. A shared CI
runner stalls; a route that is genuinely twice as slow is slow in all three samples.
That choice buys robustness at the price of sensitivity, and it is the right trade for
a gate that must not teach anyone to re-run a red build.
THE NUMBERS ARE CEILINGS, NOT TARGETS. Each `budgetMs` is what this repository is
willing to defend as BROKEN rather than as slow, on the e2e lane's own dev server.
They are generous on purpose (ADR-0007: a check blocks only where it passes), and
they are unmeasured — `baseline` is null because nothing has run the suite and
recorded what these routes actually cost. Every run attaches its measurements to the
Playwright report, so the first green CI run produces exactly the numbers a tighter
ceiling needs. TIGHTEN THEM WITH THE REASON IN THE SAME DIFF, the way every other
threshold in this repository moves; never raise one to make your own change pass —
that is rubric B3, and a perf budget is the easiest number in the tree to buy a green
with.
WHERE IT RUNS. tests/perf-budget.spec.ts, inside `npm run test:e2e` — the
`E2E smoke (Playwright, key-free)` job, which .github/required-checks.json names as a
check that may stop a change. A route over its ceiling fails that job. The registry's
own shape is held on every build by test-unit/perf-budget.test.mjs (blocking, inside
`npm run test:unit`), because a budget naming a route that no longer exists measures
nothing and says so to nobody.

metric.why: The server's answer for the route, warm, best of three — the half of a page's cost this repository's code is responsible for.

notCovered: Client bundle size and hydration cost. The dev server serves unminified chunks, so measuring them here would report on Turbopack; the honest place for that number is a budget over `next build` output, which nothing produces yet.
API route latency under load. These are single sequential navigations on an idle runner — a smoke budget, not a load test.
Production latency. The e2e lane runs the dev server; `BASE_URL=<deployment> npm run test:e2e` points the same budgets at a real deployment, where they are very generous.

routes.label: Homepage
routes.why: The marketing entry point and the most-linked page in the product. It renders the demo walkthrough, the module registry and the FAQ from fixtures — no store, no model — so a second and a half of server time here is a regression in the render path, not in the data.

routes.label: Demo app shell — portfolio overview
routes.why: The product's shop window: the whole authed shell, rendered for the anonymous sample tenant. It is the heaviest composition on the public side, and the one a visitor judges the product by.

routes.label: Campaign triage
routes.why: The heaviest READ on the public side — the campaign store under LOCAL_DB, plus the triage ranking. A store change that stops deduping its reads shows up here first.

routes.label: Winning-patterns library
routes.why: The pattern analysis runs over the same synced series on every request. It is the page where an accidental O(n²) in a pure compute helper would land.

routes.label: Free channels
routes.why: The seeded free-channel plan — the curated catalog joined to a scored plan. Cheap today, and the page most often extended by an agent adding another derived column.
